note: Hand-curated industrial pollution sources for the Vaigai basin. Each entry's source link points to documentation that specifically attributes the pollution claim being made (academic research, court records, or news coverage of pollution events). Estate listings, pin-code directories, and generic regulatory pages were dropped from earlier drafts when they didn't meet that bar.
source: Columbia GSAPP 'Water Urbanism: Madurai' studio book; Madras HC Madurai Bench (Dec 2024 PIL); India TV / news coverage of Sellur foam events.

sources.name: SIDCO industrial estate (Madurai) - Vandiyur outflow
sources.description: Per the Columbia GSAPP 'Water Urbanism: Madurai' studio book, the SIDCO industrial estate hosting rubber, steel, chemical processing, engineering, plastic, and textile units has been discharging untreated effluent into Vandiyur lake (east of Madurai city) for decades through government-authorised channels that are not regularly cleaned. The lake feeds the Vaigai system. Many of these units handle heavy metals; the channels are also reported to be clogged with plastic waste. Marker placed at Vandiyur lake, the documented receiving water body.

sources.name: Sellur sewage discharge zone
sources.description: North-bank Vaigai stretch where Nethaji Nagar, SMP Colony, Shantiniketan, Madichiyam, and Sellur dispose solid waste and raw sewage into the river. Toxic foam events have been documented on Sellur pond and the adjoining Vaigai stretch after heavy rain - surfactants from upstream effluent + stormwater agitation. The CPCB station upstream of Madurai (10059) sits roughly 1 km upstream of this zone.

sources.name: Vaigai multi-district discharge inventory (Madras HC 2024)
sources.name_ta: வைகை பல மாவட்ட கழிவுநீர் பட்டியல் (சென்னை உயர் நீதிமன்றம் 2024)
sources.operator: Madras HC Madurai Bench / TNPCB / district administrations
sources.description: In December 2024 the Madras HC took suo motu cognisance of dangerous Vaigai pollution. Submissions in court flagged 177 sewage and industrial discharge points across Madurai, Theni, Dindigul, Sivagangai, and Ramanathapuram. Water samples from 36 of those sites were classified below CPCB Class D (unfit for agriculture or industry). Hazardous shrimp-farm waste was specifically called out. The HC ordered an action plan from each district by 20 January 2025 - this multi-district inventory is the canonical 'who pollutes Vaigai where' list.
